results.title: ATO Late Lodgement Penalty: What Happens If Your Tax Return Is Late?
results.description:
The Australian Taxation Office (ATO) may apply a failure to lodge on time penalty if you miss your due date.

## Key Takeaways
- The ATO may charge a penalty for each 28-day period your return is overdue.

## When is a tax return considered late?
### ATO late lodgement fines may apply from the 31 October tax deadline
If you don’t lodge by this date, the ATO may apply a failure to lodge penalty, particularly if you don’t submit a [non-lodgement advice](https://www.etax.com.au/non-lodgement-advice/) or take steps to resolve your outstanding tax obligations.

## How much is the ATO late lodgement penalty?
**The official term for a late tax return fine is a failure to lodge on time penalty.**

## Here are the most common questions we hear about late tax returns
### “I’m afraid of owing the ATO money” or “I can’t afford to pay my overdue taxes”
Remember, if you ignore your late tax returns, ATO fines, interest and penalties can really add up.

We want to help you avoid an ATO late lodgement penalty and get the best outcome from your tax return each year.

results.title: ATO Late Lodgement Penalty: Costs and How to Avoid It - Tax Window
results.description:
If you have lodged a tax return or business activity statement late, the Australian Taxation Office can apply a Failure to Lodge penalty. For an individual or small business, this penalty starts at **$364** for being one day late and rises in steps to a maximum of **$1,820**, adding another $364 for each 28 day period the return is overdue (for documents that fell due before 1 July 2026 the penalty unit was $330, so the steps ran from $330 to $1,650).

## The Refund or Nil Result Exception
The ATO generally does not issue a Failure to Lodge penalty notice for a late lodged tax return, FBT return, annual GST return or activity statement if the lodgement results in either a refund or a nil result. In other words, if your late return would not result in any tax owing, or would actually produce a refund, the penalty is generally not charged.

## Frequently Asked Questions
### What is the penalty for lodging a tax return one day late?
For an individual or small withholder, the Failure to Lodge penalty for the first 28 day period is $364, and being just one day late falls within that first period.

### Will I get a penalty if my return results in a refund?
The ATO does not usually issue a Failure to Lodge penalty notice for a late lodged return that results in a refund or a nil result.

results.description:
# Late Tax Return Australia: 2026 Guide to ATO Penalties
## The Real Cost of Delay Deconstructing ATO Penalties
The core penalty is the **Failure to Lodge** penalty. The ATO applies **one penalty unit for each 28-day period, or part of a 28-day period, that a return is overdue, up to five units**. Each unit is **$330** for 2025 to 2026, so a single late return can move from **$330 to $1,650** depending on how long it remains outstanding, as outlined in this [ATO late tax return fine guide](https://mysupertax.com.au/blog/late-tax-return-fine-australia/).

### What the penalty actually looks like
| Time overdue | FTL penalty |
|-|-|
| **1 to 28 days** | **$330** |
| **29 to 56 days** | **$660** |
| **57 to 84 days** | **$990** |
| **85 to 112 days** | **$1,320** |
| **113+ days** | **$1,650** |

One day into the next 28-day block counts.

The penalty targets the failure to lodge on time.

## Your Next Steps with Australia Wide Tax Solutions
The failure to lodge penalty is based on penalty units ($313 per unit from 1 July 2023), accruing per 28-day period for late returns and BAS lodgements.
